ai.text:
The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 sets the rules and funding permissions for the Department of Defense's programs, activities, and military construction for that year, along with certain national security programs run by the Department of Energy.

Among its main provisions, the bill allows the military to buy various items, including aircraft and ships. It sets how many active-duty and reserve troops the military may have. It also sets policies on military health care and military pay and benefits.

The bill covers how the Department of Defense buys goods and services and manages those purchases, including the contracting powers it may use. It sets policy on the department's dealings with foreign countries, including in the Middle East, Europe, and the Indo-Pacific region. It also sets policy on cyber operations, cyber forces, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence.

The bill requires the Department of Defense to review certain materials, namely boron carbide, copper foil, and synthetic diamond. The review aims to decide what steps will keep critical defense industries supplied with these components and materials, and the department must report its findings to Congress.

The bill allows the Department of Defense's Office of Strategic Capital to make equity investments in companies outside the federal government that work on batteries and critical minerals, materials, and chemicals. It also approves specific military construction projects, extends approval for some projects from earlier years, and authorizes the National Nuclear Security Administration and the Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board.
